game_instances.player_prompt:
You are $YOUR_ROLE$.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an $GRID_SIZE$×$GRID_SIZE$ grid. Rows are labelled R1–R$GRID_SIZE$ (top to bottom), columns C1–C$GRID_SIZE$ (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and — when there are walls — a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
As a team, you must move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up; your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: $YOUR_OBJECTS$. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your $N_OTHER_PLAYERS$ teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format — no other text:
Begin your response directly with `move:` on the very first line — do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
move: <OBJECT> to R<row>,C<col> (<DIRECTION>)

Example:
move: A to R4,C3 (down)

COMMUNICATION:

The REQUEST field lets you ask your teammates to clear a cell or move out of the way. When deciding your REQUEST, also consider the reverse: is there something YOU could do — a temporary detour, a clearing move — that would unblock a teammate without being asked? Cooperation goes both ways.

move: <OBJECT> to R<row>,C<col> (<DIRECTION>)

Example:

move: A to R3,C3 (down)

DONE OPTION:
Once ALL your objects are at their target positions, you may declare done instead of making a move:
message: done
done: all my objects are placed

message: done
done: all my objects are placed

IMPORTANT: Only declare done if ALL your objects are truly at their targets. An incorrect done declaration ends the game as a failure.

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both yourself and your teammates: what do you need, and what do your teammates likely need? The best move often serves multiple goals — and when it can't, be explicit about the tradeoff in your message.

For example, (R3,C5) is row 3, column 5. Use this notation for the cells in your PLAN clause so your teammates know exactly which cells you mean.

YOUR TASK:
As a team, you must move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up; your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: $YOUR_OBJECTS$. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your $N_OTHER_PLAYERS$ teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a broadcast message. It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Your message must combine BOTH of the following, in this order:
1. Natural language (at most 100 words) — share your plan and reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or open up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you.
2. A structured plan clause at the END of the message, in exactly this form:
   PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <what you need from a teammate, or "none">
Keep the PLAN and the REQUEST short: at most 10 words each. Use (Rr,Cc) coordinates for every cell in the PLAN clause. The natural-language part and the PLAN clause may be on separate lines.

RESPONSE FORMAT:
You must respond using exactly this format — no other text:
Begin your response directly with `message:` on the very first line — do not output any preamble, thinking, or scratchpad text before it.
message: <natural language> PLAN: move <OBJECT> from (Rr,Cc) to (Rr,Cc) — REQUEST: <request or "none">
move: <OBJECT> to R<row>,C<col> (<DIRECTION>)

Example:
message: I'll work A down the left column so the middle stays open for you. PLAN: move A from (R2,C3) to (R4,C3) — REQUEST: please keep (R3,C3) clear if you can.
move: A to R3,C3 (down)

Think carefully before each move. Before choosing your move, reason about both yourself and your teammates: what do you need, and what do your teammates likely need? The best move often serves multiple goals — and when it can't, be honest about that in your message.

THE GRID:

  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).

YOUR TASK:
As a team, you must move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up; your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: $YOUR_OBJECTS$. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your $N_OTHER_PLAYERS$ teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

Before every move you must send your teammates a short broadcast message (keep it under 100 words). It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an $GRID_SIZE$×$GRID_SIZE$ grid. Rows are labelled R1–R$GRID_SIZE$ (top to bottom), columns C1–C$GRID_SIZE$ (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and — when there are walls — a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
As a team, you must move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up; your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: $YOUR_OBJECTS$. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your $N_OTHER_PLAYERS$ teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a short broadcast message (keep it under 100 words). It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now.

You are $YOUR_ROLE$.

You are playing a collaborative grid rearrangement game with your teammates.

THE GRID:
- The board is an $GRID_SIZE$×$GRID_SIZE$ grid. Rows are labelled R1–R$GRID_SIZE$ (top to bottom), columns C1–C$GRID_SIZE$ (left to right).
- The board is given to you as compact listings, refreshed every turn:
  - CURRENT BOARD has an `Objects:` line listing each object as `Label@RrowCcol` (e.g. `Objects: A@R1C1 B@R2C3`), and — when there are walls — a `Walls:` line (e.g. `Walls: R4C4 R5C6`).
  - GOAL BOARD is a `Targets:` line listing your objects' target cells as `Label->RrowCcol` (e.g. `Targets: A->R3C5`).
- Any cell not listed as an object or a wall is empty. Objects cannot enter wall cells or leave the grid.

YOUR TASK:
As a team, you must move all objects to their target positions. The GOAL BOARD shows where YOUR objects must end up; your teammates handle the rest.
You control ONLY these objects: $YOUR_OBJECTS$. You may ONLY move your own objects.
Your $N_OTHER_PLAYERS$ teammates control the remaining objects (shown as X on your board).

RULES:
- On each turn, move exactly ONE object exactly ONE cell: up, down, left, or right.
- Objects CANNOT move into wall cells or outside the grid boundaries.
- Two objects CANNOT occupy the same cell.
- You may only move objects you control.

COMMUNICATION:
Before every move you must send your teammates a short broadcast message (keep it under 100 words). It will be shown to every teammate on their next turn. Use it to share your plan AND to reflect on your teammates' situations: where do you think their objects are heading? Are you about to create an obstacle for them, or free up space they need? Acknowledge what they might need from you, even when you can't always provide it right now.
